strings: Tears of the Moon is a solemn task assigned by Priestess A'moora in the Temple of the Moon. Once cherished by the goddess Elune, the great spider Lady Sathrah has fallen into madness, forcing the Sisterhood of Elune to seek her merciful end and retrieve her sacred spinnerets.

Within the serene confines of Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora laments the tragic fate of Lady Sathrah. In earlier days, Sathrah was celebrated as a blessed creature of Elune. She wove delicate silver webs beneath the night sky, catching the evening mist that gathered upon Teldrassil's boughs. The shimmering dew her webs collected possessed miraculous healing properties, carefully gathered and preserved by the Sisterhood of Elune for their sacred ministrations.

Like much of the wildlife across the young World Tree, Lady Sathrah has recently fallen prey to an overwhelming madness. Her corruption threatens not only travelers but her own unhatched broods along the northern reaches near Wellspring Lake. Unable to cleanse her while she roams violent and frantic, the Sisterhood resolved that ending her suffering was the only compassionate path remaining. By retrieving her silvery spinnerets, the priestesses intend to dedicate her remains upon Elune's altar, praying that the Moon Goddess will grant her peace and a pure rebirth.

For the Kaldorei, putting down Sathrah is a painful reminder that the corruption touching Teldrassil's wilds spares neither the humble beast nor the sacred companions of Elune.

The Temple of the Moon is an introductory quest in Darnassus where Sister Aquinne directs adventurers to seek out Priestess A'moora. The Sisterhood of Elune requires aid for a suffering ancient creature dwelling within the boughs of Teldrassil. It serves as the opening call to a solemn ritual of mercy.

While walking among the waters and shaded groves of the Temple Gardens, travelers meet Sister Aquinne, a devoted servant of Elune. Sensing capable hands, she reaches out on behalf of her order. A venerable forest creature is suffering, and the Sisters cannot attend to the matter alone.

Sister Aquinne directs candidates toward the grand Temple of the Moon just to the southeast. There, Priestess A'moora coordinates the rituals and practical duties required to address Teldrassil's troubled wildlife, preparing sympathetic allies to carry out a sorrowful task of mercy.

For night elves, answering Sister Aquinne is an extension of their duty to protect the sacred ecosystem of Teldrassil and uphold the guidance of Elune's priesthood.

Translation to Ello is a pivotal quest in the Abercrombie storyline in Duskwood. Having asked Sirra Von'Indi to decipher the hermit's cryptic writings, the adventurer is tasked with delivering the translated parchment directly to Lord Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire.

For days, the elderly hermit Abercrombie had travelers running errands across Duskwood under the pretense of frail survival. He requested thread, preserved reagents, and personal belongings. Only when Sirra Von'Indi finally deciphers his private parchment does the truth come out: the kindly old man is an unhinged embalmer, and the components gathered were used to construct a terrifying weapon of revenge aimed straight at Darkshire.

Presenting the translated letter to Lord Ello Ebonlocke drains all color from the mayor's face. Whatever noble motives guided an adventurer's assistance, delivering those final supplies allowed Abercrombie to finish his monstrous creation, Stitches. Handing over the letter sets the behemoth marching directly eastward along the road from Raven Hill Cemetery, slaughtering any Night Watch patrols standing in its path.

Sathrah's Sacrifice is the conclusion to a somber ritual performed within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Entrusted with the remains of Lady Sathrah, players offer the fallen creature's spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters to cleanse her soul of corruption and lay her spirit to rest.

Following the tragic slaying of Lady Sathrah, Priestess A'moora charges initiates with a final spiritual duty. The great spider had fallen prey to the dark madness spreading across Teldrassil, warping her once-peaceful nature into mindless aggression. Rather than treating her death as a simple culling, the Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence. By placing her silvery spinnerets into the central fountain of the Temple of the Moon, the consecrated waters wash away the tainting corruption, granting her release.

Offering the sacrifice to Elune brings immediate spiritual communion. As the spinnerets touch the moonlit pool, the ethereal form of Lady Sathrah rises from the depths, peaceful and cleansed of the affliction that drove her mad. The Sisterhood of Elune views this ritual as necessary salvation; though the loss of the great creature is deeply felt, night elven theology teaches that through this sacred purification, she can one day be reborn with an uncorrupted spirit.

Lady Sathrah was a great spider inhabiting Teldrassil who succumbed to the creeping corruption afflicting the World Tree's wildlife. Driven mad by the taint, she had to be slain so her remains could be sanctified.

For night elves, this rite reflects their solemn duty to the flora and fauna of Kalimdor: even when creatures must be slain, their spirits are honored and cleansed through Elune's grace.

"Bride of the Embalmer" is a perilous task assigned by Lord Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire. Having pieced together the disturbing truth behind the legendary Embalmer, town leadership sends you into the haunted cemeteries of Duskwood to find his resurrected wife's resting place. By tearing the alchemist's living heart from Eliza's cursed remains, you aim to strip him of his unholy power.

For years, parents in Duskwood told their frightened children the tale of the Embalmer. According to the folktale, he was once a kindly alchemist whose mind shattered following the tragic demise of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to cheat mortality, he turned to foul sorceries and took the ultimate sacrifice: carving out his own beating heart and placing it into his wife's chest. Lord Ello Ebonlocke long dismissed this as mere village folklore, but recent revelations have proven that the Embalmer walks among them, his foul handiwork festering beneath the graveyard dirt.

The ritual succeeded in restoring Eliza to animation, but dark necromancy always demands a harrowing toll. Revived by the stolen spark of life, Eliza transformed into a ravenous abomination cursed with an insatiable hunger for living human flesh. Horrified and unwilling to destroy his creation, the Embalmer was forced to conceal his bride away in a lonely grave, visiting her in secret while plotting further depravities. To disarm the necromancer, Lord Ebonlocke directs brave souls to exhume Eliza, strike down the flesh-craving horror, and reclaim the still-pulsing organ that sustains his dark art.

When you tear the beating heart from Eliza's decomposing breast and carry it back to Darkshire, Lord Ebonlocke breathes a sigh of relief. Far from simply destroying it, the town mayor intends to turn the alchemist's dark craft against him. He believes the eldritch magic lingering within the heart will serve as a defensive talisman and aegis over Darkshire, shielding the beleaguered town from whatever wrath the weakened Embalmer might still summon in vengeance.

The Embalmer was originally an alchemist in Duskwood who went mad after his wife Eliza died. Turning to necromantic arts, he cut out his own living heart and placed it inside Eliza's corpse to resurrect her, transforming himself into an elusive monster.

Digging Through the Dirt marks the grim culmination of the hunt for the Embalmer's missing heart in Duskwood. Deep in the ravenous quiet of Raven Hill Cemetery, a disturbed mound of earth conceals a buried horror that refuses to stay dead.

Amid the countless weathered headstones of Raven Hill Cemetery sits a patch of recently turned, semi-loose soil marked with the name Eliza. While many graves in Duskwood lie desecrated by scavengers or feral ghouls, this earth was placed with deliberate intent. Digging past the topsoil reveals the splintered timber of a buried coffin, sealing away whatever remnant the Embalmer sought to hide away from the light of day.

Beneath the splintered wood lies no resting corpse. Pressing against the lid, one can feel frantic vibrations—the frantic scraping of long, clawed fingers and the hollow clatter of rotting jaws. Abercrombie's morbid experiment, Eliza, stirs violently within her pine prison, the Embalmer's missing heart beating within her breast as she waits for unwary hands to pry open the grave.

The sounds of scratching claws and gnashing teeth beneath consecrated soil are an affront to the peaceful repose promised by the Light to the deceased of Duskwood.
The Night Watch struggles constantly against the terror spilling out of Raven Hill; rooting out the buried horrors hidden by the Embalmer is vital for Darkshire's safety.

Deep within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the slumbering night elf Oben Rageclaw faces a dire magical predicament. Hostile Gnarlpine furbolg shamans have severed his dreaming spirit from his physical body, using foul enchantments to animate his flesh into a rampaging guardian.

Night elf druids enter barrow dens across Kalimdor to commune with nature through centuries of slumber, wandering the Emerald Dream while their mortal frames rest securely in stone alcoves. However, the corruption afflicting Teldrassil has driven the local Gnarlpine tribe of furbolgs to acts of desperate savagery. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans uncovered a method to breach the sanctified rest of Oben Rageclaw, prying his living spirit away from his sleeping vessel.

Rather than killing Oben, the Gnarlpine shamans used a sinister talisman—a Shaman Voodoo Charm—to forcibly animate his empty shell. Trapped helplessly in the Emerald Dream, Oben's displaced spirit can only watch as his physical form stalks the corridors, blindly attacking any who enter the den. To unravel the enchantment and find a path toward restoring his body, his ethereal projection tasks adventurers with retrieving one of the Gnarlpine charms for study.

Mercenaries is a bounty contract issued by Magistrate Bluntnose in Thelsamar to cull the encroaching Mo'grosh ogres in northeastern Loch Modan. With military reinforcements from Ironforge bogged down in months of bureaucratic delay, the magistrate is forced to hire passing adventurers to protect the valley's vulnerable settlements, excavations, and the vital Stonewrought Dam.

Thelsamar is feeling the sting of dwarven bureaucracy. It took two full months for Ironforge to even promise a handful of soldiers to bolster Loch Modan's local defense, and another two months before those troops are slated to arrive. With town guards stretched to their limits, Magistrate Bluntnose cannot afford to wait four months while hostile forces mass just beyond the valley's borders.

The Mo'grosh ogres have fortified an encampment in the hills northeast of the loch. Their growing presence jeopardizes not just the town of Thelsamar, but the Ironband Excavation Site and the Stonewrought Dam itself. Should the dam be attacked or compromised, the devastation downstream would be catastrophic. Lacking official mountaineer detachments, Bluntnose has turned to freelance mercenaries to thin out the ogre ranks and buy the valley time against both ogres and troggs.
Why is Magistrate Bluntnose hiring mercenaries instead of using guards?

Ironforge has been agonizingly slow to respond to Loch Modan's pleas for aid. It took two months for the Senate to approve sending even a handful of soldiers, and another two months until they actually arrive. Facing immediate threats to Thelsamar, the dam, and local dig sites, Bluntnose has no choice but to pay independent adventurers.

With military defense practically nonexistent and the Mo'grosh ogres establishing a camp nearby, Bluntnose fears an organized raid could damage or sabotage the massive structure, unleashing catastrophic floods.

Seeing the crown jewel of dwarven engineering—the Stonewrought Dam—left unguarded due to Ironforge red tape makes Bluntnose's call to arms a personal matter for any mountaineer or traveler from the capital.

A bounty posted in Thelsamar by Magistrate Bluntnose calls for the death of Chok'sul, an ogre warlord menacing northeastern Loch Modan. Believed to be organizing the assaults against local settlements and critical infrastructure, bringing his head secures a handsome reward from the town's leadership.

While troggs and wildlife constantly test the borders of Loch Modan, the arrival of organized ogres represents an escalation that the local dwarven mountaineers cannot ignore. Settling into encampments along the rugged northeastern reaches of the valley, these brutes have moved beyond simple scavenging. According to local scouts and town authorities, their raids are focused, persistent, and dangerous.

Thelsamar's Magistrate Bluntnose identified Chok'sul as the mastermind coordinating the violence against the town, the nearby dwarven excavation site, and the Stonewrought Dam itself. Fearing catastrophic damage to the valley's prized engineering feat and civilian lives, the magistrate placed a bounty upon the ogre chieftain: dead through any means necessary, with his severed head required as proof.

The Stonewrought Dam is one of the greatest feats of dwarven civil engineering ever constructed; allowing brute ogres to damage it is unthinkable to any respectable craftsman.

Deep within the barrows of Teldrassil, the spectral form of Oben Rageclaw asks for a tragic release. Corrupted furbolgs have placed a dark enchantment over his physical vessel, forcing you to destroy his soulless shell and break the bond so his spirit may return to the Emerald Dream.

While resting in the barrows beneath Teldrassil, Oben Rageclaw suffered a terrible fate. The corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs subjected his slumbering body to a foul voodoo enchantment, severing his spirit from his mortal flesh. Trapped in the Emerald Dream, Oben's spirit lingers nearby, unable to rest or reclaim his own body.

Examining the Gnarlpine's voodoo charm revealed the grim truth: Oben's physical shell is entirely under the furbolgs' dominion. To break the enchantment, an adventurer must enter the nearby chamber, strike down the mindless, hostile husk of Oben Rageclaw, and use the furbolg charm over his remains to finally shatter the magic binding his soul.
Why do I have to kill Oben Rageclaw?
